attack: C8 fire 2: clean-only (zero-contamination) dielectric physics-vs-ML-vs-stack pipeline on RadonPy PI1070, escalating fire 1's contaminated-train/clean-test-slice (n=20) probe into a fully clean train+calib+test pipeline (n_clean=113).

pre_registered_refute_criterion.criterion_a: ML test R2 <= 0 on the clean-only pipeline (no better than predicting the mean)
pre_registered_refute_criterion.criterion_b: paired bootstrap (n_boot=2000, seed=0) 90%% CI of (physics_MAE - ML_MAE) on the clean test set includes zero
pre_registered_refute_criterion.logic: EITHER criterion refutes the claim that ML's apparent large advantage over Onsager physics (shipped KPI, fire-1 full-population: physics R2=-1.67 vs ML R2=+0.64) is real predictive skill rather than an artifact of scoring against 89.5%-corrupted labels at large n.

split: clean-only plain random 60/20/20 (seed=0), n_train=67, n_calib=22, n_test=24 -- RF retrained FROM SCRATCH on clean-train only (fire 1's RF was trained on the full 89.5%-corrupted population and only test-sliced to n=20 clean rows)

comparison_to_fire1.interpretation: Training the RF from scratch on ONLY the physically-valid rows (n_train=67) rather than the full 89.5%-corrupted population removes the large-n advantage that let ML fit the corrupted majority's low-variance near-electronic-limit values. This isolates whether ML's edge over physics reflects genuine chemical-structure-to-dielectric-constant skill or simply exploiting the corrupted population's homogeneity.
